Bacillus species isolated from evergreen oaks are not only phenotypically and genotypically heterogeneous but also exhibit different spatial distribution on leaves.
B. pumilis and B. circulan are the dominant species on evergreen leaf surfaces, while B. cereus is the most common species on littered leaves.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the leaf surface may serve as a reservoir of spore-forming bacteria that are capable of surviving and proliferating on the leaf surface.
